messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Omeprazole usually takes 1 to 4 days of once-daily dosing to reach Omeprazole's full effect.
Some people get complete relief of their symptoms within 24 hours.
Omeprazole begins reducing stomach acid within about 1 hour of the first dose.
Omeprazole is not designed to relieve heartburn right away.
What to expect after you start taking omeprazole:
Within 1 hour: omeprazole starts to reduce acid production in your stomach
Around 2 hours: a single dose reaches Omeprazole's strongest acid-lowering effect
Within 24 hours: some people get complete relief of their symptoms
1 to 4 days: most people feel the full benefit
About 4 days: the acid-lowering effect reaches Omeprazole's maximum with once-daily dosing
How fast does omeprazole start working?
:
Omeprazole starts working within about 1 hour.
A single dose has Omeprazole's strongest effect at around 2 hours.
Omeprazole is when the medicine begins lowering acid production.
This is not the same as when your heartburn or acid reflux symptoms stop.
Omeprazole does not work immediately on symptoms you are already feeling.
Triples: [["Omeprazole", "has administration instruction", "once-daily dosing"], ["Omeprazole", "takes time to reach full effect", "1 to 4 days"], ["Omeprazole", "has time to reach full effect", "1 to 4 days"], ["Omeprazole", "starts reducing stomach acid", "within about 1 hour of first dose"], ["Omeprazole", "not designed to relieve", "heartburn immediately"], ["Omeprazole", "has time for strongest acid lowering effect", "around 2 hours"], ["Omeprazole", "has time for complete symptom relief", "within 24 hours"], ["Omeprazole", "has time for maximum acid lowering effect", "about 4 days with once-daily dosing"], ["Omeprazole", "starts working", "within about 1 hour"], ["Omeprazole", "has strongest effect at", "around 2 hours"], ["Omeprazole", "begins lowering acid production", "when medicine begins"], ["Omeprazole", "not same as", "symptoms stopping"], ["Omeprazole", "does not work immediately on", "current symptoms"]]
Relations: ["begins lowering acid production", "does not work immediately on", "has administration instruction", "has strongest effect at", "has time for complete symptom relief", "has time for maximum acid lowering effect", "has time for strongest acid lowering effect", "has time to reach full effect", "not designed to relieve", "not same as", "starts reducing stomach acid", "starts working", "takes time to reach full effect"]
Answer:

completion:
begins lowering acid production: The subject drug starts to lower acid production at the time specified by the object entity.  
does not work immediately on: The subject drug does not provide relief for the symptoms specified by the object entity immediately.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug is administered according to the instruction specified by the object entity.  
has strongest effect at: The subject drug reaches its strongest effect at the time specified by the object entity.  
has time for complete symptom relief: The subject drug provides complete symptom relief after the time specified by the object entity.  
has time for maximum acid lowering effect: The subject drug reaches its maximum acid-lowering effect after the time specified by the object entity.  
has time for strongest acid lowering effect: The subject drug reaches its strongest acid-lowering effect after the time specified by the object entity.  
has time to reach full effect: The subject drug takes the time specified by the object entity to reach its full effect.  
not designed to relieve: The subject drug is not intended to relieve the condition specified by the object entity.  
not same as: The subject drug's effect is not the same as the event or condition specified by the object entity.  
starts reducing stomach acid: The subject drug begins to reduce stomach acid at the time specified by the object entity.  
starts working: The subject drug begins to take effect after the time specified by the object entity.
